items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Sterling Way was the manager there. ... I went up to Sterling Way and I said, 'Well,' I said, 'here we are. Stuff Smith's here and Joe Comfort's here and there isn't anything you can do about it, baby.'

ctx.x: But the time when you couldn't play it was when it was operated as a full time band place where the Palladium hired the bands. When you later played it didn't you say that you played for another promoter?

Oh, yeah. Sterling Way was the manager there. We played a private party in there and we had been playing -- well, I played the Palladium when it was a week's job, and then I also played it when it was five days, and then I played it when it got down to three, and I played it when

it got down to two. One of these times when we were down, I think it was to three days a week they were going, one other day there we played an engagement for City College of Los Angeles, and I had Stuff Smith there and Joe Comfort in the band, and I went up to Sterling Way and I said, "Well," I said, "here we are. Stuff Smith's here and Joe Comfort's here and there isn't anything you can do about it, baby." And he said, "Well, it isn't me anyway. It's the policy of the owners."
